class ledger.era.conway.ConwayBlockBody.note: the transactions and the size and hash of the segments the body was read from, made only from a block's bytes (ConwayBlock.decode), where the reference keeps the four segments' bytes and their hash; ConwayBbodySuite's expectations are the reference's own only on the 53 recorded Conway blocks the reference accepted

def ledger.era.conway.ConwayBlock.decode.note: a block's bytes as the flat block decoder reads them, its header and body in the era's types; ConwayBbodySuite's expectations are the reference's own only on the 53 recorded Conway blocks the reference accepted

def ledger.era.conway.ConwayBlock.inputs.note: every input of the block's transactions (allInputsTxBodyF) less those a transaction of the block creates; the node's read set of a Conway block from the store

def ledger.era.conway.ConwayBlock.read.note: a block's bytes as the flat block decoder reads them, a Conway block's header and body also in the era's types, read once for the rules of its era; decode is its Conway case; ConwayBbodySuite runs the era block

def ledger.era.conway.ConwayBlockBody.of.note: the body in Conway's types from the body the flat block decoder read from a block's bytes, each transaction read by Conway's decoders, the size and hash the decoder computed from the same segments; ConwayBbodySuite's expectations are the reference's own only on the 53 recorded Conway blocks the reference accepted

val ledger.era.conway.ConwayBlockBody#ha.note: the hash of the segments the decoder computed (hashAlonzoSegWits); ConwayBbodySuite's expectations are the reference's own only on the 53 recorded Conway blocks the reference accepted

val ledger.era.conway.ConwayBlockBody#si.note: the segments' length, what encCBORGroup writes; ConwayBbodySuite's expectations are the reference's own only on the 53 recorded Conway blocks the reference accepted

val ledger.era.conway.ConwayBlockBody#tx.note: ConwayBbodySuite's expectations are the reference's own only on the 53 recorded Conway blocks the reference accepted

val ledger.era.conway.ConwayBlockBody.in.note: blockBodySize the segments' length, which encCBORGroup writes again at every version; ConwayBbodySuite's expectations are the reference's own only on the 53 recorded Conway blocks the reference accepted

val ledger.era.conway.ConwayBlockHeader..note: the Praos header's instance of EraBlockHeader with its protocol version (PraosEraBlockHeader), over the header the block decoder read with its fields read once in the classes' types; ConwayBbodySuite's expectations are the reference's own only on the 53 recorded Conway blocks the reference accepted

glue.reason: The Conway switch (#85): the node's one reading of a block's bytes for the rules of its era (Prepared, and ConwayBlock.Read, the block decoder's reading beside the era block made from it), why the node reaches no verdict on a Conway block its era rules apply (ConwayBlockDefect), and the node's phase-2 counters added field by field (PlutusStats' Monoid). The reference reads a block once and has no verdict-less outcome or such counters; these are Scarab's own.

the companions and readers of Conway's block in the era's types, as Dijkstra's: the header's fields read once in the classes' types (ConwayBlockHeader, a plain class so that no Mirror builds one whose fields are not its header's, its fields, rendering and reader), the evidence that a flat block is one the block decoder read (ConwayBlock.Decoded, which only ConwayBlock.decode makes), why a block's bytes are not a Conway block in the era's types, by whose the failure is (ConwayBlockError and its total classification ConwayBlockError.of), a body's rendering, the object of the Praos header class; the gate of the header's version from the build (HeaderProtVerGate.of), as WithdrawalsRule.of; and a BBODY test's failures injected into the rule's (bbodyTest), which the reference's ?! injectFailure does
